display.purpose: The product value of a roll, in Lucky Gold. The largest and heaviest type in the interface. Die numerals sit just under it at 700 / 1.8rem in the same gold.

headline.purpose: The wordmark only, filled with a 135 degree Iris-to-Gold gradient clipped to the text.

title.purpose: Card headings. Small enough that a card reads as a panel rather than a page section.

body.purpose: The default, and the input value size, so a typed stake matches the surrounding text weight exactly.

label.purpose: Table column headers, uppercased and tracked. Field labels use the same family at 0.85rem in Fog, sentence case.

shadows.name: card-ambient
shadows.purpose: On every card, always identical. Separates the surface from the ground without implying hierarchy.

shadows.name: action-glow
shadows.purpose: Primary button hover only, paired with a 1px lift. The only colored shadow in the system.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Inputs on focus, with the border shifting to Iris at the same time.

shadows.name: toast-float
shadows.purpose: The one genuinely floating element, slightly heavier than a card.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Every pointer response: hover, focus, border and background shifts, the 1px lift.

motion.name: roll
motion.purpose: Die tiles on every result. Full 360 degree Y rotation with the scale dipping to 0.8 at the halfway point; values swap in at 200ms so numbers change mid-flip.

motion.name: balance-pop
motion.purpose: The balance pill confirming that money moved.

motion.name: toast-slide
motion.purpose: Toast entering from 100px below and leaving the same way after a 3 second hold.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The roll action. Full width, one per card, the only element that visibly rises off the surface.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 100%; padding: 0.75rem 2rem; border: none; border-radius: 8px; background: var(--primary, #6c5ce7); color: #fff; font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--primary-hover, #7f70f0); transform: translateY(-1px); box-shadow: 0 4px 12px rgba(108, 92, 231, 0.4); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(108, 92, 231, 0.2); } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Quick Pick
components.description: A popular predicted product with its real win probability underneath. Shown at rest, selected, and in the best-odds variant that wears Gold.
components.css: .ds-picks { display: flex; gap: 0.4rem; flex-wrap: wrap; } .ds-pick { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; min-width: 52px; padding: 0.4rem 0.7rem; border: 1px solid var(--border, #2a2e3e); border-radius: 8px; background: var(--bg, #0f1117); color: var(--text, #e4e6eb); font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 0.9rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.2; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.2s; } .ds-pick small { font-size: 0.65rem; font-weight: 400; color: var(--text-muted, #8b8fa3); } .ds-pick:hover { border-color: var(--primary, #6c5ce7); background: var(--surface-hover, #22263a); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-pick:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(108, 92, 231, 0.2); } .ds-pick--active { border-color: var(--primary, #6c5ce7); background: rgba(108, 92, 231, 0.2); color: #fff; } .ds-pick--best { border-color: var(--accent, #ffd32a); background: rgba(255, 211, 42, 0.08); } .ds-pick--best:hover { border-color: var(--accent, #ffd32a); background: rgba(255, 211, 42, 0.2); }

components.name: Quick Stake
components.description: Adds a fixed amount to the stake field. Teal because it puts money on the table, and tighter cornered than a pick so the two rows do not read alike.
components.css: .ds-stakes { display: flex; gap: 0.4rem; } .ds-stake { padding: 0.3rem 0.6rem; border: 1px solid var(--border, #2a2e3e); border-radius: 6px; background: var(--bg, #0f1117); color: var(--success, #00b894); font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.2s; } .ds-stake:hover { border-color: var(--success, #00b894); background: rgba(0, 184, 148, 0.1); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-stake:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(0, 184, 148, 0.25); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Stake and prediction fields. Filled with the page ground so the control reads as punched into the card.
components.css: .ds-field { font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; } .ds-field__label { display: block; margin-bottom: 0.3rem; font-size: 0.85rem; color: var(--text-muted, #8b8fa3); } .ds-field__input { width: 100%; padding: 0.7rem 1rem; border: 1px solid var(--border, #2a2e3e); border-radius: 8px; background: var(--bg, #0f1117); color: var(--text, #e4e6eb); font-family: inherit; font-size: 1rem; transition: border-color 0.2s; } .ds-field__input:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--primary, #6c5ce7); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(108, 92, 231, 0.2); }

components.name: Card
components.description: The only container in the system. Every card carries the same border and the same ambient shadow, whatever it holds.
components.html:
Place Your Bet

Cards stack in one 900px column with a 1.5rem gap.
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--surface, #1a1d27); border: 1px solid var(--border, #2a2e3e); border-radius: 12px; padding: 1.5rem; box-shadow: 0 4px 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3); font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; color: var(--text, #e4e6eb); } .ds-card__title { margin: 0 0 1rem; font-size: 1.1rem; font-weight: 600; } .ds-card__body { margin: 0; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.6; color: var(--text-muted, #8b8fa3); }

components.name: Dice Equation
components.description: The signature component. Three die tiles read as arithmetic across to the product, with the roll animation replayed on every result. Hover the tiles to see the roll.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-equation { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.7rem; flex-wrap: wrap; font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; } .ds-die { width: 64px; height: 64px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; background: var(--bg, #0f1117); border: 2px solid var(--border, #2a2e3e); border-radius: 12px; font-size: 1.8rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--accent, #ffd32a); transition: transform 0.3s; } .ds-equation:hover .ds-die { animation: ds-roll 0.4s ease-in-out; } @keyframes ds-roll { 0% { transform: rotateY(0deg) scale(1); } 50% { transform: rotateY(180deg) scale(0.8); } 100% { transform: rotateY(360deg) scale(1); } } .ds-op { font-size: 1.3rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--text-muted, #8b8fa3); } .ds-product { min-width: 60px; font-size: 2rem; font-weight: 800; color: var(--accent, #ffd32a); text-align: center; }

components.name: Balance Pill
components.description: The player's money, in the header. Scales to 1.1 for 300ms whenever the balance changes, which is how the system confirms a transaction.
components.css: .ds-identity { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 1rem; font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; } .ds-identity__name { font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--text-muted, #8b8fa3); } .ds-balance { min-width: 100px; padding: 0.4rem 1rem; border-radius: 20px; background: var(--primary, #6c5ce7); color: #fff; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 700; text-align: center; transition: transform 0.2s; } .ds-identity:hover .ds-balance { transform: scale(1.1); }

components.name: Outcome Badge
components.description: The won/lost and credit/debit pair. Always full-strength text on a 15% tint of its own color, never a solid fill.
components.html: WONLOST🎉 WON!
components.css: .ds-badges { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 1rem; font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; } .ds-badge { display: inline-block; padding: 0.15rem 0.6rem; border-radius: 12px; font-size: 0.8rem; font-weight: 600; } .ds-badge--won { background: rgba(0, 184, 148, 0.15); color: var(--success, #00b894); } .ds-badge--lost { background: rgba(225, 112, 85, 0.15); color: var(--danger, #e17055); } .ds-status { padding: 0.3rem 1.2rem; border-radius: 20px; font-size: 1.3rem; font-weight: 700; } .ds-status--won { background: rgba(0, 184, 148, 0.15); color: var(--success, #00b894); border: 1px solid var(--success, #00b894); }

components.name: History Tabs
components.description: Local navigation inside the history card. Text only, on a hairline rule, with a 2px Iris underline marking the active tab.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; gap: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border, #2a2e3e); font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; } .ds-tab { padding: 0.7rem 1.5rem; border: none; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; background: none; color: var(--text-muted, #8b8fa3); font-family: inherit; font-size: 0.95rem; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.2s; } .ds-tab:hover { color: var(--text, #e4e6eb); } .ds-tab:focus-visible { outline: none; color: var(--text, #e4e6eb); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(108, 92, 231, 0.2); } .ds-tab--active { color: var(--primary, #6c5ce7); border-bottom-color: var(--primary, #6c5ce7); }

narrative.overview:
The room is dark and the instruments are on. Surfaces are Midnight Slate and its two lighter siblings, hairline borders separate everything, and the type is the operating system's own UI face at rest. Then three dice land in Lucky Gold and the terminal admits, briefly, that it is a casino. That contrast is the whole system: a composed readout that keeps one warm light burning over the table.

It is precise and composed first. Values are exact, the rhythm repeats, controls answer in two tenths of a second with a single pixel of lift, and nothing is approximate. But it is not solemn. The wordmark carries a die, results land with an emoji, the best-odds pick wears a star, and the quick picks tell you your real chance of winning before you spend anything. The system knows it is a dice game and is willing to say so, as long as it says so in the same measured voice it uses for the ledger.

Depth is tonal, never dramatic. The palette is disciplined about meaning: violet is the only color that acts, gold is the only color that rolls, and teal and clay only ever report an outcome. Confirmed rejections: this system does not become neon slot-machine chrome (gradient bevels, glow spam, confetti, coin shine), and it does not become a crypto trading terminal (tickers, sparklines, wall-to-wall red and green, manufactured urgency).
keyCharacteristics: One 900px column of stacked cards on a Midnight Slate ground, with a single breakpoint at 600px.
A three-step tonal ramp does all structural depth work; the one card shadow is atmosphere.
Controls are punched into the card, not raised off it. Only the primary action rises.
Gold has exactly three homes, all of them the game itself.
Zero font requests. Zero image requests. The only artwork is a 5-pip SVG favicon.
Every state change is 0.2s, with a 1px lift and a colored glow on the primary action.

rules.name: The Iris Means Action Rule
rules.body: Violet marks what the visitor can do and who they are. If an element is not actionable, not focused, and not the balance, it does not get Iris.

rules.name: The Gold Only Rolls Rule
rules.body: Lucky Gold has three homes: the numerals of a roll, the product they make, and the pick marked best. Adding a fourth costs the first three their meaning.

rules.name: The Outcome Pair Rule
rules.body: Teal and Clay report results and nothing else. They never become brand colors, never decorate, and never appear on an element whose meaning is not won/lost or credit/debit.

rules.name: The Zero-Request Type Rule
rules.body: The system loads no font files. Type costs nothing at first paint today, and a webfont is a trade to argue for rather than a default to reach for.

rules.name: The Weight Before Size Rule
rules.body: Emphasis is bought with weight (600, 700, 800) before it is bought with size. Only the roll result is allowed to be both.

rules.name: The Single Column Rule
rules.body: Everything below the header is one column of cards at one measure. The bet row is the only place the system nests a grid, and it collapses at the single breakpoint.

rules.name: The Tone Ramp Rule
rules.body: Structural depth comes from Midnight, Surface and Raised. Shadow never ranks importance and never gets heavier to make something matter more.

rules.name: The Inset Control Rule
rules.body: Anything that accepts input recedes to Midnight Slate with a Slate Line border. Only the primary action rises off the surface, and it rises in Iris.

rules.name: The Shared Corner Rule
rules.body: Cards and dice both take 12px, so a rolled die reads as a small card rather than a foreign object dropped into the layout.

rules.name: The Pill Means Status Rule
rules.body: The 20px pill is reserved for things that report a live value: the balance and the won/lost verdict. Actions never wear it.

rules.name: The Two-Tenths Rule
rules.body: Every state change runs 0.2s. Only events are allowed longer: the roll at 0.4s, the toast at 0.3s, the balance pop at 300ms. If it responds to a pointer, it is 0.2s.

rules.name: The One Loud Thing Rule
rules.body: Each card gets at most one element at full saturation: the Iris button in the bet card, the Gold product in the result card, the badges in the history. Everything else in that card is neutral.

dos: Do keep Lucky Gold on the game. Its three homes are the die numerals, the product, and the best-odds pick.
Do recess controls into Midnight Slate with a 1px Slate Line border, and let only the primary action rise.
Do answer every pointer in 0.2s with a 1px lift. Crisp, with a spring in it.
Do hold the 900px single column and let the one 600px breakpoint collapse the bet row and shrink the dice.
Do reserve Teal and Clay for won/lost and credit/debit, always as a 15% tint under full-strength text.
Do pair every quick pick with its real win probability. Telling the visitor their odds is part of the voice.
Do keep type on the system stack unless a webfont earns the request it costs.
donts: Don't drift into neon slot-machine chrome: no gradient bevels, glow spam, confetti, sparkles, or coin shine on the gold.
Don't drift into a crypto trading terminal: no tickers, no sparklines, no wall-to-wall red and green numerals, no manufactured urgency.
Don't rank importance with shadow. Every card carries the same ambient shadow; depth is tonal.
Don't give Iris a second job. It means action, focus and identity, never decoration.
Don't put two full-saturation elements in one card.
Don't introduce a second colored shadow. The Iris action glow is the only one.
Don't use the 20px pill for anything actionable; it belongs to live values.
